title: a row a person decided stays decided
line: the first row of a FamilySearch 1950 census search fits Frederick Micheal Ahearn and is a lead for its own record; accepted by the owner as him, the row stays accepted and its record is still the lead, since it is not yet fetched; neither a plan run nor the rule undoes the link; rejected by the owner as him, it stays rejected and is no lead for him: a person's decision is never undone

steps.say: a 1950 citation on the person, planted: the file cites none on him, so the step stands with its record id on the owner's word

step.rationale: harness: a 1950 citation on the owner's word; fetch the record at United States, Census, 1950

steps.say: the search saved: the first row fits him and is a lead
the owner's word that the row is his, as a card an older matcher put to it would leave the link
his plan regenerated, then the rule re-examines everything: the link stays accepted, no card is written for any row, and the row's record is still a lead

expect.why: accepted as him, the row's own record is not yet fetched: still the lead
a person's own decision is never undone by the rule
and no card is written for any row

steps.say: the owner's word that the row is not him
his plan regenerated: a row rejected as him is no lead for him, and the link stays rejected

expect.why: the plan drops the lead it never ran
